title: India-Pakistan Ceasefire First Anniversary: Competing Victory Narratives, Zero Diplomatic Contact — Bilateral Freeze Intact at One Year
detail: The first anniversary of the May 10, 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire — which ended the Operation Sindoor / Marka-e-Haq military exchange — passed on May 10, 2026 with both capitals holding competing victory commemorations and zero bilateral diplomatic contact. India's Air Force posted a commemorative video on X marking the exact hour of the May 7, 2025 strikes, featuring BrahMos cruise missile footage and images of destroyed Pakistani radar sites. PM Modi declared India 'remains steadfast to demolish the terror ecosystem' and changed his social media profile pictures to imagery from Operation Sindoor. J&K Police DGP Prabhat stated on May 10 that J&K Police are 'fighting Pakistan-sponsored terrorism' with close synergy among security forces. Pakistan held its Marka-e-Haq national victory ceremonies as the culmination of a week-long anniversary information campaign (Corps Commanders' Conference May 5, book launch May 6, DG ISPR press conference May 7, anniversary documentary May 8, Islamabad security operations May 9). Pakistan Air Force held a ceremony at Nur Khan Auditorium in Rawalpindi honoring the PAF's role in May 2025. Al Jazeera captured the bilateral dynamic in a piece titled 'Two wins, two losses: What India and Pakistan have learned a year after war.' The bilateral freeze remained fully intact: Indian and Pakistani airspace mutually closed until May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all direct trade halted, no ambassadors exchanged.

title: Analysis: Pakistan's Rapid Post-Conflict Rearmament — Army Rocket Force Command Operational, Taimoor Tested, J-35A Pipeline Active at One-Year Mark
detail: Quwa Defence News & Analysis published a detailed assessment on May 10-11, 2026 cataloguing Pakistan's rapid military rearmament in the twelve months since the Marka-e-Haq ceasefire. Key developments: Pakistan formally operationalized its Army Rocket Force Command (ARFC), which manages the Fatah-3 precision surface-to-surface rocket system (range 400+ km), Shaheen ballistic missiles, and loitering munitions — creating a dedicated conventional precision-strike branch paralleling India's Rocket Force. The Pakistan Air Force confirmed in January 2026 the first successful flight test of the Taimoor air-launched cruise missile (600 km range, terrain-following profile, launched from Mirage IIIE); the Pakistan Navy conducted a live Taimoor naval-variant firing in April 2026. Pakistan's procurement pipeline includes up to 40 J-35A/J-35AE stealth fighters from China (signed June 2025, estimated delivery 2027-2028) and expansion of J-10CE and JF-17 Block III fleets. Asia Times assessed that J-35AE deliveries to Pakistan 'risk nuclear escalation with India.' The Diplomat published 'A Year After Operation Sindoor: Rising Risks and Deepening Instability,' warning that unresolved root causes — cross-border terrorism, Kashmir, Indus Waters — make conflict re-ignition a significant risk. Pakistan's ARFC operationalization is assessed as a significant structural change to South Asian conventional balance.

media.caption: Analysis: Pakistan's rapid military rearmament one year after Marka-e-Haq — Army Rocket Force Command, Taimoor cruise missile, J-35A stealth fighters
